subject.title: [Feature]: Automatically install brew if not installed

question: Should OpenClaw skill onboarding be allowed to bootstrap Homebrew automatically when brew-backed dependencies are missing?
rationale: The requested behavior would move from showing a command to executing external package-manager bootstrap code during setup, which is a security and product-policy choice rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Keep guidance-only default
options.body: Preserve the current safe default and improve in-product guidance or recovery surfaces without running Homebrew bootstrap code automatically.

options.title: Approve explicit opt-in bootstrap
options.body: Allow bootstrap only behind clear user consent, platform limits, verified command/provenance, timeout/logging, and tests for onboarding and direct install paths.

options.title: Defer to package authors
options.body: Keep core out of Homebrew installation and require skills/plugins to provide maintained non-brew installers or setup documentation.

recommendation.title: Keep guidance-only default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current safe default and improve in-product guidance or recovery surfaces without running Homebrew bootstrap code automatically.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest feature-history owner for the Homebrew onboarding and Linuxbrew resolver behavior that this decision would change.
